- Overestimate prices in the short term after recent sentiment spikes (positive sentiment → model tends to overshoot).
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently negative over recent days → model underreacts to bearish signals.
- Model tends to lag in correcting downward trends; true prices often dip below forecast before rebounding.
- When sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model delays upward correction — forecast lags the sentiment shift.
- In high-sentiment periods (especially >0.3), model overreacts to short-term volatility, leading to over-forecasting in early days of the horizon.
- Model underestimates long-term price drift (30d) when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative — fails to capture gradual upward momentum.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., 80→85) — model overcorrects downward, then fails to recover fully.
- Mean reversion bias: model often forecasts prices to revert to historical mean too quickly, ignoring sentiment-driven momentum.
- Sentiment-driven momentum is not fully captured in 30d forecasts — model underweights sentiment when it’s trending strongly.
